nodes.title: Kloosterman sums
nodes.statement: For a finite field F of q elements, an additive character ψ:F→C× and n≥0, set RawKl_{n+1}(a;ψ)=Σ_{x∈(F×)^n} ψ(Σ_i x_i+a/(Π_i x_i)), for a∈F×. For F/F_p use ψ=ψ_p∘Tr_{F/F_p}, where ψ_p is nontrivial. The empty product defines RawKl_1(a)=ψ(a). The exported all-rank sheaf interface assumes r=n+1≥2.
hypotheses: F a finite field; ψ_p nontrivial when claiming Weil or monodromy conclusions.
All summation coordinates and a are units.
proofSteps: Use the pinned additive-character and finite-field trace carriers.
Index the finite sum by functions Fin n→F×; prove reindexing and trace-extension identities by finite-sum congruence.

Apply Deligne’s Kloosterman direct-image construction; concentration and the !→* comparison are part of the target, not definitions by assertion.

nodes.title: Cohomology of Kloosterman moments

Define the middle space as im(H_c¹→H¹); it is pure of weight k+1, and its determinant polynomial is M_k. nodes.title: Integrality of moment polynomials
nodes.statement: For every k≥1 and prime p, each m_2^k(p^m) is a rational integer independent of the nontrivial prime-field additive character, and Z_k(p;T) belongs to Z[T] with constant term one. gaps.title: Generic preservation of similitude forms under semisimplification
gaps.detail: The needed general statement is now pinned directly to Serre Theorem 4.2.1, pp. 9–10, read with its proof. A maximal isotropic submodule gives an anisotropic semisimple quotient and a paired hyperbolic summand; this produces the same symmetric or alternating type on the semisimplification. G7 has the symmetric-power polarization API but no exact node found for this theorem for algebras with involution. The request specifies it and the χ_cyc-twisted group-algebra involution; add it to that owner as a Part II extension, not as another Kloosterman theorem.

gaps.title: Higher-thickness semistable model in the bad-prime comparison
gaps.detail: The existing RD.7 Mieda node requires each local equation over Z_p[sqrt(−p)] to be Q−u(sqrt(−p))² with u a unit. The expansion in FSY (5.6)/(5.16) has constant 2ap/2bp. For example k=9,p=3,a=3 gives constant 18 of valuation two, not one; p may divide the orbit parameter. The assertion on FSY p. 50 does not verify this unit hypothesis. A resolution for arbitrary thickness, a stronger comparison theorem, or another proof of semistability and Frobenius compatibility is required. The good-prime crystalline branch and the all-prime de Rham assertion do not use this step. Record source issue E9 and the limitation of the imported RD.7 node; do not silently treat it as an unconditional supplier.
